speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is experiencing bilious vomiting and has not passed meconium yet; can you tell me exactly how many hours old the baby is when these symptoms first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant have a family history of cystic fibrosis or other genetic conditions, and was a prenatal ultrasound performed to check for bowel dilation? I need to know if there were any signs of intestinal obstruction detected before birth.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-ray
REQUEST TEST: Rectal Biopsy

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Rectal Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.
